to_task: Quantitative three-gain nonconcentration and transfer to Landau coercivity or hydrodynamic limits
goal_and_scope: Determine exactly what the N58 seven-coordinate rank lemma proves and whether it yields quantitative, Landau, or hydrodynamic conclusions.
inherited_inputs: Fixed-scale/sign axial cold profiles, nonaxial endpoint, hard-sphere gain map
Bounded parameter densities, source kernel/tail/compactness/axis lemmas, and finite-temperature C1 convergence
Grazing kernel with angular second moment bounded below
acquired_inputs: Full-rank slab counterexample to any universal rate under convergence-in-measure-only input
Order-delta^(-2) divergence of the positive hot generator under grazing normalization
Primary Landau and hydrodynamic literature comparison
representation_and_assumptions: Phi_3 maps 12 collision parameters to (t3,x3,v3) in seven dimensions. Rank seven almost everywhere yields qualitative nonconcentration under compact truncation, bounded densities and C1 convergence. Quantitative estimates require a uniform minor lower bound and input L1 modulus. Landau/hydrodynamic transfers require separate signed operator, entropy, scaling, conservation and compactness estimates.
exact_missing_lemma: For Landau, a delta-uniform off-axis lower bound for the complete signed Landau linearization with cold-parent loss included, preserving nonnegative total density and controlled entropy production. For quantitative N58, a critical-set sublevel modulus and explicit input L1 decay rate. For hydrodynamics, a specified scaling plus uniform moment/entropy compactness, local conservation and limit identification; for particle fluctuations, horizon/data/graph-size-uniform recollision and centering bounds.
comparator: Pinned OA363 five-gain rank lemma; N58 lowers it to three, the minimum for this parameterization. Primary literature derives Landau/hydrodynamic limits using entropy production, properly scaled solutions and conservation/correlation estimates.
falsifier_or_next_experiment: Test the full signed Landau linearization on one fixed smooth separated compact pair and off-axis observable under standard grazing normalization; a uniform lower bound would be necessary but not sufficient. For a quantitative rank theorem, bound the measure of the least-singular-value sublevel set and the input L1 rate.
